core: Definition of the software development life cycle (SDLC) as a phased process
Standard phases: requirements/planning, design, implementation, testing/verification, deployment, operation and maintenance
Process models: waterfall (sequential), iterative/incremental, agile (e.g., Scrum)
Why a defined process matters: risk management, coordination, cost of fixing defects late
ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 as the authoritative life cycle standard
supporting: Agile Manifesto four values and preference for short iterations and change
Scrum sprints as fixed-length iterations timeboxed to one month or less
Boehm's finding that defect-fix cost rises the later a defect is found
outOfScope: Debugging technique (finding/fixing specific defects) — named, owned by the debugging topic
Decomposition of problems into parts — named, owned separately
Algorithm design and how to write code — used inside implementation, owned separately

claims.claim: The SDLC is a structured, phased process for planning, building, delivering, and maintaining software, standardized as a framework of life cycle processes by ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 spanning acquisition, development, operation, maintenance, and disposal.
The standard phases run requirements/planning, then design, then implementation (coding), then testing/verification, then deployment, then operation and maintenance.

The waterfall model runs the phases once in a strict sequence, completing and signing off each before the next begins; iterative/incremental models repeat the phases in cycles that each produce a working version.

The 2001 Agile Manifesto states four values: individuals and interactions over processes and tools; working software over comprehensive documentation; customer collaboration over contract negotiation; and responding to change over following a plan. Agile teams favor short iterations, delivering working software frequently, and welcoming changing requirements even late in development.
Scrum, the most common agile framework, organizes work into fixed-length iterations called sprints, timeboxed to one month or less.
The cost of fixing a software defect rises sharply the later in the life cycle it is discovered, per Barry Boehm's studies of large projects; catching defects early therefore reduces cost and risk.

Security is more effective and cheaper when integrated into every SDLC phase rather than added at the end; NIST SP 800-218 (SSDF) recommends secure development practices woven throughout the life cycle.
No process model is universally best; waterfall suits stable, well-understood requirements with heavy documentation needs, while agile suits changing requirements and fast feedback.

positions: Boehm's 1981 data suggested roughly 1x/5x/10x/20x/100x across requirements to post-release
Later commentators note the precise multipliers vary widely by project, context, and study and should not be treated as universal constants
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Stated qualitatively in the lesson: cost 'rises sharply' and is 'often by roughly an order of magnitude or more,' attributed to Boehm, without asserting a fixed numeric law.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft contained only generic filler ('a foundational concept... a simple way to apply it') with no substantive, verifiable claims about the SDLC, its phases, or its models.
correctionsNeeded: Replaced boilerplate that never named the phases with the actual ordered phases (requirements through maintenance).
Added the three process models (waterfall, iterative/incremental, agile/Scrum) presented neutrally, which the draft omitted entirely.
Added the risk/coordination/cost-of-late-defects rationale and the ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 and NIST references, none of which the draft included.
Rewrote vague vocabulary (e.g., 'context', 'evidence') into SDLC-specific terms.

sourceRecords.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207-2017 — Systems and software engineering — Software life cycle processes
sourceRecords.notes: Read the IEEE SA public description page and cross-checked the ISO abstract (iso.org/standard/63712.html returned 403 to the fetcher; scope confirmed via IEEE SA page and search of the ISO catalog entry) on 2026-08-19. Supports that 12207 establishes a common framework of software life cycle processes with defined terminology, covering acquisition, supply, development, operation, maintenance, and disposal; published 2017-11-15. Used only for scope and authority; no standard text reproduced. Cited for the definition and phase framing.

sourceRecords.title: Manifesto for Agile Software Development
sourceRecords.provider: Beck, Beedle, van Bennekum, Cockburn, Cunningham, Fowler, et al.
sourceRecords.license: Freely copyable in entirety per the manifesto's own notice; authors retain copyright
sourceRecords.notes: Read via WebFetch 2026-08-19 (main page and principles.html). Confirms the four values verbatim (individuals and interactions over processes and tools; working software over comprehensive documentation; customer collaboration over contract negotiation; responding to change over following a plan) and the 17 signatories, 2001. Principles page confirms 'welcome changing requirements, even late in development' and delivering working software frequently 'from a couple of weeks to a couple of months, with a preference to the shorter timescale.' Supports the agile values, short-iteration and change claims. Only the four short value statements are quoted.

sourceRecords.title: The Scrum Guide (2020)
sourceRecords.notes: Verified via web search of the official 2020 Scrum Guide 2026-08-19. Supports that Scrum organizes work into fixed-length iterations called Sprints, timeboxed to one month or less, with Sprint Planning, Review, and Retrospective events. Used for the single factual detail about sprints; described in original prose.

sourceRecords.title: NIST SP 800-218: Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1
sourceRecords.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sourceRecords.notes: Read via WebFetch 2026-08-19. U.S. government work, public domain. Supports that most SDLC models do not explicitly address security, and that SSDF recommends integrating a core set of secure software development practices into each phase of any SDLC to reduce vulnerabilities. Published February 2022; authors Souppaya, Scarfone, Dodson. Cited for the security-across-the-life-cycle point.

sourceRecords.title: Handbook of Software Engineering Methods
sourceRecords.provider: Oregon State University Open Educational Resources
sourceRecords.notes: License confirmed via curl (CC BY-NC) and content via search/summary 2026-08-19; the agile chapter (open.oregonstate.education/setextbook/chapter/agile/) returned 403 to the fetcher but the book overview and search results confirm coverage. Supports the description of waterfall as linear/sequential with signed-off phase documents, iterative development producing a working version each cycle, agile emphasizing iterative development and customer collaboration, and the general principle that defects found later cost more (Boehm). Facts synthesized into original prose; attributed here.
